function.name: delegate_task
function.description:

1. Single task: provide 'goal' (+ optional context, toolsets)
2. Batch (parallel): provide 'tasks' array with up to 3 items. All run concurrently and results are returned together.

WHEN TO USE delegate_task:
- Reasoning-heavy subtasks (debugging, code review, research synthesis)
- Tasks that would flood your context with intermediate data
- Parallel independent workstreams (research A and B simultaneously)

WHEN NOT TO USE (use these instead):
- Mechanical multi-step work with no reasoning needed -> use execute_code
- Single tool call -> just call the tool directly
- Tasks needing user interaction -> subagents cannot use clarify

- Subagents have NO memory of your conversation. Pass all relevant info (file paths, error messages, constraints) via the 'context' field.
- Subagents CANNOT call: delegate_task, clarify, memory, send_message, execute_code.
- Each subagent gets its own terminal session (separate working directory and state).
- Results are always returned as an array, one entry per task.

context.description: Background information the subagent needs: file paths, error messages, project structure, constraints. The more specific you are, the better the subagent performs.

toolsets.description: Toolsets to enable for this subagent. Default: inherits your enabled toolsets. Common patterns: ['terminal', 'file'] for code work, ['web'] for research, ['terminal', 'file', 'web'] for full-stack tasks.

tasks.description: Batch mode: tasks to run in parallel (limit configurable via delegation.max_concurrent_children, default 3). Each gets its own subagent with isolated context and terminal session. When provided, top-level goal/context/toolsets are ignored.

function.name: execute_code
function.description:
Run a Python script that can call Hermes tools programmatically. Use this when you need 3+ tool calls with processing logic between them, need to filter/reduce large tool outputs before they enter your context, need conditional branching (if X then Y else Z), or need to loop (fetch N pages, process N files, retry on failure).

Use normal tool calls instead when: single tool call with no processing, you need to see the full result and apply complex reasoning, or the task requires interactive user input.

Available via `from hermes_tools import ...`:

  read_file(path: str, offset: int = 1, limit: int = 500) -> dict
    Lines are 1-indexed. Returns {"content": "...", "total_lines": N}
  write_file(path: str, content: str) -> dict
    Always overwrites the entire file.
  search_files(pattern: str, target="content", path=".", file_glob=None, limit=50) -> dict
    target: "content" (search inside files) or "files" (find files by name). Returns {"matches": [...]}
  patch(path: str, old_string: str, new_string: str, replace_all: bool = False) -> dict
    Replaces old_string with new_string in the file.
  terminal(command: str, timeout=None, workdir=None) -> dict
    Foreground only (no background/pty). Returns {"output": "...", "exit_code": N}

Limits: 5-minute timeout, 50KB stdout cap, max 50 tool calls per script. terminal() is foreground-only (no background or pty). If the session uses a cloud sandbox backend, treat it as resumable task state rather than a durable always-on machine.

Print your final result to stdout. Use Python stdlib (json, re, math, csv, datetime, collections, etc.) for processing between tool calls.

Also available (no import needed — built into hermes_tools):
  json_parse(text: str) — json.loads with strict=False; use for terminal() output with control chars
  shell_quote(s: str) — shlex.quote(); use when interpolating dynamic strings into shell commands
  retry(fn, max_attempts=3, delay=2) — retry with exponential backoff for transient failures

code.description: Python code to execute. Import tools with `from hermes_tools import terminal, ...` and print your final result to stdout.

function.name: terminal
function.description:
Execute shell commands on a Linux environment. Filesystem usually persists between calls.

Do NOT use cat/head/tail to read files — use read_file instead.
Do NOT use grep/rg/find to search — use search_files instead.
Do NOT use ls to list directories — use search_files(target='files') instead.
Do NOT use sed/awk to edit files — use patch instead.
Do NOT use echo/cat heredoc to create files — use write_file instead.
Reserve terminal for: builds, installs, git, processes, scripts, network, package managers, and anything that needs a shell.

Foreground (default): Commands return INSTANTLY when done, even if the timeout is high. Set timeout=300 for long builds/scripts — you'll still get the result in seconds if it's fast. Prefer foreground for short commands.
Background: Set background=true to get a session_id. Two patterns:
  (1) Long-lived processes that never exit (servers, watchers).
  (2) Long-running tasks with notify_on_complete=true — you can keep working on other things and the system auto-notifies you when the task finishes. Great for test suites, builds, deployments, or anything that takes more than a minute.
Use process(action="poll") for progress checks, process(action="wait") to block until done.
Working directory: Use 'workdir' for per-command cwd.
PTY mode: Set pty=true for interactive CLI tools (Codex, Claude Code, Python REPL).

Do NOT use vim/nano/interactive tools without pty=true — they hang without a pseudo-terminal. Pipe git output to cat if it might page.
Important: cloud sandboxes may be cleaned up, idled out, or recreated between turns. Persistent filesystem means files can resume later; it does NOT guarantee a continuously running machine or surviving background processes. Use terminal sandboxes for task work, not durable hosting.

command.description: The command to execute on the VM

background.description: Run the command in the background. Two patterns: (1) Long-lived processes that never exit (servers, watchers). (2) Long-running tasks paired with notify_on_complete=true — you can keep working and get notified when the task finishes. For short commands, prefer foreground with a generous timeout instead.

timeout.description: Max seconds to wait (default: 180, foreground max: 600). Returns INSTANTLY when command finishes — set high for long tasks, you won't wait unnecessarily. Foreground timeout above 600s is rejected; use background=true for longer commands.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command (absolute path). Defaults to the session working directory.

check_interval.description: Seconds between automatic status checks for background processes (gateway/messaging only, minimum 30). When set, I'll proactively report progress.

pty.description: Run in pseudo-terminal (PTY) mode for interactive CLI tools like Codex, Claude Code, or Python REPL. Only works with local and SSH backends. Default: false.

notify_on_complete.description: When true (and background=true), you'll be automatically notified when the process finishes — no polling needed. Use this for tasks that take a while (tests, builds, deployments) so you can keep working on other things in the meantime.

function.name: text_to_speech
function.description: Convert text to speech audio. Returns a MEDIA: path that the platform delivers as a voice message. On Telegram it plays as a voice bubble, on Discord/WhatsApp as an audio attachment. In CLI mode, saves to ~/voice-memos/. Voice and provider are user-configured, not model-selected.

text.description: The text to convert to speech. Keep under 4000 characters.

output_path.description: Optional custom file path to save the audio. Defaults to ~/.hermes/audio_cache/<timestamp>.mp3

function.name: todo
function.description:
Manage your task list for the current session. Use for complex tasks with 3+ steps or when the user provides multiple tasks. Call with no parameters to read the current list.

Writing:
- Provide 'todos' array to create/update items
- merge=false (default): replace the entire list with a fresh plan
- merge=true: update existing items by id, add any new ones

Each item: {id: string, content: string, status: pending|in_progress|completed|cancelled}
List order is priority. Only ONE item in_progress at a time.
Mark items completed immediately when done. If something fails, cancel it and add a revised item.

Always returns the full current list.

todos.description: Task items to write. Omit to read current list.

merge.description: true: update existing items by id, add new ones. false (default): replace the entire list.

- CEO Agent - strategic delegation and oversight
- Specialist Agents: coder, engineer, designer, writer, researcher, sales,
  security, customer-support, brand-advocacy, presentations, saas-operations
- Heartbeat Agent - monitors system health and inter-agent communications
- Antigravity Agent - experimental/special tasks

Delegation Hierarchy:
  Bob (Human) -> Main -> CEO -> Specialists
                             ^-- Heartbeat (monitors all)
"""

import os
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

OPENCLAW_HOME = Path(os.environ.get('OPENCLAW_HOME', '/home/bob/.hermes/.openclaw'))
AGENTS_DIR = OPENCLAW_HOME / 'agents'
WORKSPACES = {
    'main': OPENCLAW_HOME / 'workspace-main',
    'ceo': OPENCLAW_HOME / 'workspace-ceo',

AGENT_DESCRIPTIONS = {
    'main': 'Communications agent. Interfaces with Bob and coordinates specialist delegation. Handles presentations and writing.',

}


def build_agent_prompt(agent_id: str, task: str, context: str = '') -> str:
    """Build a self-contained prompt for a specific agent with its full context."""
    agent_dir = AGENTS_DIR / agent_id / 'agent'

    # Read agent definition files
    soul = ''
    identity = ''
    agent_md = ''
    skill = ''

    for fname, var in [('SOUL.md', 'soul'), ('IDENTITY.md', 'identity'),
                        ('AGENT.md', 'agent_md'), ('SKILL.md', 'skill')]:
        path = agent_dir / fname
        if path.exists():
            content = path.read_text()
            if fname == 'SOUL.md': soul = content
            elif fname == 'IDENTITY.md': identity = content
            elif fname == 'AGENT.md': agent_md = content
            elif fname == 'SKILL.md': skill = content

    prompt = f"""You are the {agent_id.title()} Agent in the OpenClaw multi-agent system.

<agent_definition>
{agent_md or f'Agent ID: {agent_id}'}
</agent_definition>

<identity>
{identity or f'Role: {AGENT_DESCRIPTIONS.get(agent_id, "Specialist agent")}'}

<soul>

<skill>

{task}

Begin execution now.

    return prompt

    return MODELS.get(agent_id, 'qwen/qwen3.6-plus')


def agent_list() -> list:
    return list(AGENT_DESCRIPTIONS.keys())

{"content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
OpenClaw Delegation Engine
===========================
Uses Hermes delegate_task to run OpenClaw agents in parallel.
"""

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from datetime import datetime, timezone

sys.path.insert(0, '/home/bob/.hermes/openclaw_emulation')
from openclaw_core import AGENT_DESCRIPTIONS, build_agent_prompt, get_workspace, get_model, agent_list

OPENCLAW_HOME = Path('/home/bob/.hermes/.openclaw')


def auto_select_agents(task: str) -> list:
    """Auto-select the best agents for a task based on keywords."""
    task_lower = task.lower()
    selected = set()
    
    keyword_map = {
        'design': ['designer', 'engineer'],
        'ui': ['designer'],
        'image': ['designer'],
        'visual': ['designer'],
        'code': ['coder', 'engineer'],
        'script': ['coder'],
        'implementation': ['coder', 'engineer'],
        'build': ['coder', 'engineer'],
        'develop': ['coder', 'engineer'],
        'write': ['writer'],
        'content': ['writer'],
        'book': ['writer', 'content:writer'],
        'article': ['writer'],
        'copy': ['writer', 'brand-advocacy'],
        'research': ['researcher'],
        'analyze': ['researcher'],
        'investigat': ['researcher'],
        'market': ['researcher', 'sales'],
        'competitor': ['researcher'],
        'trend': ['researcher'],
        'sale': ['sales'],
        'lead': ['sales'],
        'prospect': ['sales'],
        'outreach': ['sales', 'brand-advocacy'],
        'security': ['security'],
        'vuln': ['security'],
        'audit': ['security'],
        'scan': ['security'],
        'support': ['customer-support'],
        'ticket': ['customer-support'],
        'faq': ['customer-support'],
        'brand': ['brand-advocacy'],
        'social': ['brand-advocacy'],
        'present': ['presentations'],
        'pitch': ['presentations'],
        'demo': ['presentations'],
        'saas': ['saas-operations'],
        'subscription': ['saas-operations'],
        'operat': ['saas-operations'],
        'infrastructure': ['engineer', 'saas-operations'],
        'architect': ['engineer'],
        'strategy': ['ceo'],
        'plan': ['ceo'],
    }
    
    for keyword, agents in keyword_map.items():
        if keyword in task_lower:
            for a in agents:
                clean = a.split(':')[-1]
                selected.add(clean)
    
    # Always route through main for coordination
    selected.add('main')
    
    return list(selected)[:5]  # Cap at 5 agents


def run_delegation(task: str, agents: list = None, from_agent: str = 'main', context: str = '') -> dict:
    """Run the delegation engine and return the plan."""
    
    if agents:
        selected = [a for a in agents if a in AGENT_DESCRIPTIONS]
    else:
        selected = auto_select_agents(task)
    
    # Build delegation plan
    plan = {
        'timestamp': datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        'from_agent': from_agent,
        'task': task,
        'selected_agents': selected,
        'routing': []
    }
    
    for agent_id in selected:
        workspace = get_workspace(agent_id)
        model = get_model(agent_id)
        
        # Save task file
        tasks_dir = Path(workspace) / 'tasks'
        tasks_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        
        ts = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime('%Y%m%d_%H%M%S')
        task_file = tasks_dir / f'delegate_{ts}_{agent_id}.md'
        task_content = f"""# Delegated Task

**From:** {from_agent}
**To:** {agent_id}
**Time:** {task_file.parent.name}
**Model:** {model}

## Task
{task}
"""
        task_file.write_text(task_content)
        
        plan['routing'].append({
            'agent': agent_id,
            'model': model,
            'workspace': workspace,
            'task_file': str(task_file),
            'prompt_chars': len(build_agent_prompt(agent_id, task, context)),
        })
    
    return plan


def print_delegation_plan(plan: dict):
    """Pretty-print the delegation plan."""
    print("\n" + "="*60)
    print("  OPENCLAW - DELEGATION PLAN")
    print("="*60)
    print(f"  Task:     {plan['task'][:100]}")
    print(f"  From:     {plan['from_agent']}")
    print(f"  Agents:   {', '.join(plan['selected_agents'])}")
    print(f"  Time:     {plan['timestamp']}")
    print("="*60)
    
    for route in plan['routing']:
        print(f"\n  -> {route['agent']}")
        print(f"     Model:     {route['model']}")
        print(f"     Workspace: {route['workspace']}")
        print(f"     Task file: {route['task_file']}")
        print(f"     Prompt:    {route['prompt_chars']} chars")
    
    print("\n" + "="*60 + "\n")


if __name__ == '__main__':
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        print("Usage: python delegate.py 'task description' [--agents a,b,c]")
        sys.exit(1)
    
    task_parts = []
    agents_override = None
    i = 1
    while i < len(sys.argv):
        if sys.argv[i] == '--agents':
            agents_override = sys.argv[i+1].split(',')
            i += 2
        else:
            task_parts.append(sys.argv[i])
            i += 1
    
    task = ' '.join(task_parts)
    plan = run_delegation(task, agents_override)
    print_delegation_plan(plan)

# Telegram Gateway Troubleshooting

Use when: `send_message` to Telegram fails, the gateway logs show Telegram errors, cron jobs report delivery failures, or test messages don't arrive.

## Diagnostic Steps

### 1. Verify Gateway is Running
```bash
systemctl status hermes-gateway.service --no-pager
```

### 2. Check Gateway Logs for Errors
```bash
journalctl -u hermes-gateway.service --no-pager -n 30 | grep -i telegram
```

Common errors and their meanings:
- `httpx.ReadError` — network/HTTP disconnect; the gateway auto-reconnects (up to 10 attempts)
- `terminated by other getUpdates request` — multiple long-polling clients hitting the same bot; only one can poll at a time
- `chat not found` — the chat_id has never started a conversation with the bot, or the user blocked it
- `Bad Request` — invalid message format, markdown parse error, or entity issues
- `bot was kicked from the supergroup` — bot was removed from a chat
- `Forbidden: bot was blocked by the user` — user blocked the bot

### 3. Verify Bot Token is Valid and Not Masked
```bash
# Check the actual token value (NOT the masked *** placeholder)
grep '^TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=' ~/.hermes/.env

# Test the token directly
TOKEN=$(grep '^TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=' ~/.hermes/.env | cut -d= -f2-)
curl -s "https://api.telegram.org/bot${TOKEN}/getMe"
```

Expected: `{"ok":true,"result":{"id":...,"is_bot":true,...}}`

Pitfall: The `.env` file may have literally `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=***` as placeholder. The real token is set in `.openclaw/openclaw.json` or was placed after initial setup. Always read the actual value with `cut` — never trust grep display alone.

### 4. Check if Chat ID is Reachable
```bash
TOKEN=$(grep '^TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=' ~/.hermes/.env | cut -d= -f2-)
curl -s "https://api.telegram.org/bot${TOKEN}/sendMessage" \
  -d "chat_id=<CHAT_ID>" \
  -d "text=Test"
```

If you get `Bad Request: chat not found`:
- The user has NEVER sent a message to the bot. Bots CANNOT initiate conversations.
- Fix: Tell the user to open Telegram, search for the bot (e.g., `@FLBobBot`), and send any message like "hi".
- Then re-verify: `curl -s "https://api.telegram.org/bot${TOKEN}/getUpdates?limit=3"`

### 5. Check Allowed Users Configuration
```bash
# Hermes gateway allowed users
grep 'TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS\|GATEWAY_ALLOW' ~/.hermes/.env

# OpenClaw allowed users
cat ~/.openclaw/credentials/telegram-default-allowFrom.json
```

If `TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS` is empty and `GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS=false`, all incoming messages are rejected (but outbound messages to known chat IDs still work).

### 6. Check for Polling Conflicts
```bash
TOKEN=$(grep '^TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=' ~/.hermes/.env | cut -d= -f2-)
curl -s "https://api.telegram.org/bot${TOKEN}/getUpdates?limit=1"
```

If you get `Conflict: terminated by other getUpdates request`:
- Multiple processes are long-polling the same bot.
- The Hermes gateway handles this gracefully (auto-reconnects), but other OpenClaw instances or manual scripts may conflict.
- Only the gateway should be doing long polling. Kill any other process using the token.

### 7. Check Recent Telegram Updates (Who Has Contacted the Bot)
```bash
TOKEN=$(grep '^TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=' ~/.hermes/.env | cut -d= -f2-)
curl -s "https://api.telegram.org/bot${TOKEN}/getUpdates?limit=10"
```

This shows which users the bot can actually message. You can only send messages to users who have initiated a conversation first.

### 8. Fix Common Issues

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| Token = `***` literal | Run `hermes setup` or manually set `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=actual_token_here` in `~/.hermes/.env` |
| User needs to start chat | Tell user: "Open Telegram, search for @BotName, send 'hi'" |
| Wrong chat_id in config | Update `TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS` in `~/.hermes/.env` |
| Network errors | These auto-recover; check DNS and firewall only if persistent |
| Polling conflict | Ensure only one process (gateway) is doing long-polling |
| Markdown parse error in messages | Use `parse_mode=HTML` or escape markdown chars |

## Quick Test Command
```bash
TOKEN=$(grep '^TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=' ~/.hermes/.env | cut -d= -f2-)
curl -s "https://api.telegram.org/bot${TOKEN}/sendMessage" \
  -d "chat_id=8137891480" \
  -d "text=Test from Hermes $(date)"
```
